content.title: The Score: Tyson, Robinhood, Walmart, Paramount Skydance and More Stocks That Defined the Week
content.summary: Chicken sales are helping offset Tyson’s beef losses as the American cattle shortage takes a bite out of  Tyson’s  profits.  The meatpacking giant on Monday said its beef prices rose 17% in the latest quarter, while beef sales volumes fell 8% amid the lowest U.S. cattle supply since the 1950s.  As price tags rise on beef and pork products, consumers are flocking to chicken nuggets and wings, helping lift Tyson’s chicken sales.

content.title: Bitcoin Slides To 6-Month Low Amid Hawkish Fed Turn
content.summary: The bitcoin price continued its sharp fall for a second day, hitting a six-month low early Friday but coming off its lows.  The fall in the cryptocurrency and stocks such as Strategy and Coinbase Global comes as markets react to a hawkish shift in Federal Reserve policymaker comments raising doubt about an interest-rate cut next month, despite labor market softness.  Bitcoin's sell-off appears to have added another worry for stock market investors amid concern that financial engineering had begun to propel the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, including Magnificent Seven stocks like Nvidia.

content.title: Don’t Call Them Bets. They’re ‘Prediction Markets’—and Robinhood Is Getting Rich Off Them.
content.summary: “Will the U.S. say that aliens exist this year?”  Robinhood Markets  clients can currently guess “yes” through their brokerage app, paying $4, plus $2 in fees, to win $100 if they’re right.  If I’ve been abducted and probed by extraterrestrials, is it inside information?  Robinhood  prefers terms like “prediction markets” and “event trading.”
